predecessors.name: Principality of Iberia
predecessors.text: Kakheti, Kukheti and Gardabani, which Grigol separated from the Principality of Iberia

successors.name: Kingdom of Georgia
successors.text: Kakheti and Hereti, annexed by David IV in 1104 and divided into the Duchy of Kakheti, the Duchy of Hereti, the Khornabuji bank and the Land of Arishini

ledger.x: 1014: Kvirike III recovers his crown after Bagrat III's death.

c. 1014: Kvirike III unites Kakheti and Hereti and crowns himself king. The kingdom 'emerged in c. 1014 AD' under Kvirike III 'who united Kakheti and Hereti'; the infobox places the Hereti incorporation in the 1010s and the Principality page gives 1010 as the union.

c. 1014: the chorepiscopal principality becomes the Kingdom of Kakheti-Hereti. Kvirike III 'crowned himself king' and 'made Telavi his capital'; David (976-1010) was the last to hold the chorepiscopal title.
1104: Aghsartan II is handed to David IV and the kingdom falls.
1104: Kakheti-Hereti ends as a state and its lands become Georgian duchies.

wars.name: Constantine III and Kvirike I against Hereti
wars.outcome: Kvirike I allied with Constantine III of Abkhazia, invaded Hereti and the allies divided its major strongholds.

wars.name: Abkhazian overlordship over Kakheti
wars.outcome: Padla II aided George II of Abkhazia in 925; under Kvirike II the Abkhazian king raided Kakheti and in 959 Kvirike's brother Shurta handed him Ujarma; 'Kakheti later reclaimed its lands after a truce with Leon III'.

wars.name: Sajid invasions of Kakheti
wars.outcome: 'Sajid invasions in 914 and 936 caused losses'; Hereti's king then reclaimed fortresses from Kakheti.

wars.name: Bagrat III's conquest of Kakheti
wars.outcome: Bagrat III defeated David of Kakheti in 1008, invaded in 1010 and captured Kvirike III; Kakheti was recovered after Bagrat's death in 1014.

wars.name: Kakhetian-Georgian war against Fadhl II of Arran (Eklez River)
wars.outcome: Gagik's forces joined Bagrat IV's against Fadhl II of Arran, who was defeated at the Eklez River in 1027.

wars.name: Seljuk submission and invasion of Kakheti-Hereti
wars.outcome: Aghsartan I submitted to Alp Arslan and agreed to pay tribute in 1068, fought Malik-Shah I's invasion in 1074 and embraced Islam and pledged loyalty to the Seljuks in the early 1080s.

wars.name: David IV's annexation of Kakheti and Hereti
wars.outcome: Heretian nobles seized Aghsartan II and handed him to David IV, who annexed the kingdom; the lands became duchies under the Arishiani governor.

certainty.note: The Kingdom page names rivers (Ksani, Alijanchay, Mtkvari) but no survey line; Kakheti's western Kartli border moved often.
